newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue chips end up on year-end window dressing.
newsitem.headline: KL blue chips end up on year-end window dressing.

text.p: Malaysian blue chips soared on the last trading session of 1996 on year-end window dressing, but activity remained muted ahead of the New Year holiday, dealers said.
The Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks closed up 23.27 points or 1.92 percent at 1,237.96. For the year, the index was up 24.4 percent from 995.17 at end-1995.

"It's year-end dressing. Given the thin market volume, the index could have gone even higher," said an analyst with a foreign brokerage house. He said strong buying emerged in the last hour of trading.
Secondary stocks, however, gave back most of their early gains on profit-taking.
The Second Board index ended the year at 576.31, up 0.68 points. It was up a hefty 93 percent for the year.
Market volume was 183 million shares, with gainers beating losers 310 to 280.
Major gainers included Tenaga Nasional, Malayan Banking, Malaysian Airline System, Proton and Edaran Otomobil Nasional which rose between 20 cents and 1.25 ringgit.
Leading the day's volume was newly listed Johor Land. The stock closed at 4.42 ringgit against an offer price of 2.20.
